documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, age 47.

Saw ID in April - he says it went fine, numbers good, same pills; we never got a note. Neuro not since last August, he plans to call. GI: still on nifedipine, nothing else planned.

No new complaints. Weight steady. Smoking the same; not interested in medication to quit, patch is enough for him. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Alert, in no distress. Oral mucosa pink, no lesions. Neck without adenopathy. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen benign. Skin: no rash, no lesions on legs or trunk. Rises from chair using arms. No edema.

Health maintenance:
- FIT again this year, kit given.
- Tdap today; no record of one.
- Shingrix complete 2022. PCV20 2021.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, UA.
- Lung screening: from age 50.

RTC fall for shots.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in because of purple spots. For several weeks he has had dark purple spots on the roof of his mouth and on both lower legs. Not painful. Also a dry cough that won't quit, several weeks, no blood. Waking up soaked at night. Pants are loose - down about 7 kg since last year on our scale. No fever he knows of. Still taking his HIV pill every day.

O: Vitals as charted; weight 71.0 kg (78 last spring). Thin. Several violaceous macules and papules on the hard palate. Multiple similar purple papules on both shins and calves, non-blanching. No adenopathy felt in the neck or axillae. Lungs: clear to auscultation, no crackles. Heart regular. Abdomen soft.

A/P: violaceous skin and palate lesions with cough, night sweats and weight loss in a man with AIDS. Kaposi sarcoma is high on the list; infection needs to be excluded too.
- Urgent dermatology referral for biopsy - called and got him in on 2/19.
- CT chest ordered.
- CBC, CMP today.
- Messaged his ID clinic, they will move his visit up.
- Return precautions for fever or shortness of breath.
I'll call with results.

documents.title: ID clinic notified
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called ID clinic nurse line per PCP, relayed lesions, cough, weight loss, night sweats. They will see pt 2/27 with labs and want derm and CT results faxed.

reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING CENTER
CT chest without contrast.
Indication: chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats; HIV.
Comparison: none.

Findings: Bilateral perihilar infiltrates. Small bilateral pleural effusions. No pneumothorax. Central airways patent. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal mass. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. Bones without suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral perihilar infiltrates with small bilateral pleural effusions.

documents.title: CT chest result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT: bilateral perihilar infiltrates and small effusions. Called pt - discussed, no fever or dyspnea. Faxed to derm and ID ahead of their visits. Labs from 2/6 fine.

events.reason: Violaceous lesions of hard palate and lower extremities

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, left lower leg, 4 mm punch biopsy.
Microscopic: dermal proliferation of spindle-shaped cells forming slit-like vascular spaces, with neovascularization and extravasated red blood cells.
Comment: diagnostic of Kaposi sarcoma in this clinical setting.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY
Date of service: 02/19/2024
Referred urgently by PCP.

48-year-old man with HIV on ART and achalasia, seen for purple lesions of the palate and legs. He also has a dry cough lasting weeks, with weight loss and drenching night sweats over the same period.

Allergies: penicillin (rash).
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF, nifedipine ER 30 mg, acetaminophen prn, nicotine patch.

Exam: numerous red-violet papules that do not blanch, on the hard palate and over both lower legs.
Chest CT from 02/13 reviewed: bilateral perihilar infiltrates, small effusions.

Procedure: 4 mm punch biopsy, left lower leg, after consent; hemostasis with pressure, one suture.

Pathology (02/22): spindle cell proliferation with new vessel formation and red cells outside the vessels - Kaposi sarcoma.

Assessment: Kaposi sarcoma involving skin and oral mucosa; the chest CT raises concern for lung involvement.
Plan: urgent oncology referral placed; ID aware. Suture out in 10 to 14 days at PCP or here.

Dermatology

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC
Visit date: 02/27/2024

Seen sooner than planned for biopsy-proven Kaposi sarcoma of skin and palate, with perihilar infiltrates and small effusions on CT, cough, night sweats and weight loss.

Adherent to bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF.
CD4 291 cells/uL. HIV-1 RNA not detected (<20 copies/mL).

Assessment: KS despite viral suppression. Infection must be excluded as a cause of the lung findings before they are attributed to KS. Pulmonary referral for bronchoscopy with BAL arranged; oncology referral already placed by dermatology. CD4 above 200: no PJP prophylaxis.
Plan: continue ART unchanged through chemotherapy, no interactions of concern with liposomal doxorubicin. Labs again in 6 months.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Suture removal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Single suture removed from left lower leg biopsy site. Site clean and healed, no drainage. Pt has bronchoscopy next week and oncology the week after.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with Bronchoalveolar Lavage
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY - BRONCHOSCOPY REPORT
Date of procedure: 03/07/2024
Indication: bilateral perihilar infiltrates and small effusions in a man with HIV and newly diagnosed cutaneous/oral Kaposi sarcoma; exclude infection.
Allergies: penicillin.
Sedation: moderate, monitored.

Findings: vocal cords normal. Trachea and main bronchi patent. Airway mucosa without focal lesion. Scant clear secretions.
BAL right middle lobe, returns clear.

BAL results (final 03/13): bacterial culture no growth. AFB smear negative; AFB culture no growth so far, final at 6 weeks. Pneumocystis stain negative.

Impression: no infection identified on BAL. Results to oncology and ID.
No complications; discharged home same day.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY
Date of service: 03/12/2024

Reason: Kaposi sarcoma, referred by dermatology.

History: HIV on ART with suppressed viral load, CD4 291 last month. Several weeks of red-violet lesions on the palate and lower legs, punch biopsy 02/19 Kaposi sarcoma. Dry cough, night sweats, weight loss of about 7 kg. CT chest 02/13: bilateral perihilar infiltrates with small pleural effusions. Bronchoscopy 03/07 with BAL negative for bacteria, AFB and Pneumocystis.
Other history: hereditary myopathy, achalasia on nifedipine ER, tobacco use (35 pack-years, current), remote IVDU in remission.
Allergies: penicillin (rash).

Exam: palate and bilateral lower-leg violaceous papules as described. Lungs clear. No hepatosplenomegaly.

Assessment: AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma involving skin and oral mucosa, with pulmonary involvement - with infection excluded, the perihilar infiltrates and effusions are attributed to KS. Systemic therapy indicated.

Plan: liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks, 6 cycles, starting 03/18/2024. Continue ART per ID. CBC before each cycle here. Restaging CT chest after cycle 6. Discussed hair, mouth sores, low counts, hand-foot reaction, infusion reactions.

Oncology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Interval: bronch BAL negative for infection; oncology calls the lung findings KS along with skin and palate. Cycle 1 of liposomal doxorubicin 3/18. Tired for a few days after, appetite ok, no fever. Next cycle 4/8. Still smoking about a pack a day, patch on.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight holding since February. Palate and shin lesions unchanged in appearance. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema. Biopsy site healed.

A/P:
- Kaposi sarcoma (skin, palate, lung) - on liposomal doxorubicin per oncology; CBCs there. Fever = call oncology same day.
- HIV - ART unchanged per ID.
- Achalasia - nifedipine ER, soft diet is helping him keep weight on.
- Myopathy - unchanged.
- Tobacco - encouraged cutting down during treatment.
RTC after chemo course, around August.

OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY
Date of service: 07/01/2024

Cycle 6 of 6 liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 given today; course complete.

Tolerated treatment with fatigue only; no delays. Counts adequate before each cycle.
Skin and palate lesions are now flat and faded. Cough has resolved; no night sweats for about two months. Weight coming back.

Plan: restaging CT chest in 4-5 weeks. Surveillance visits every 6 months after that. Continue ART.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after finishing 6 cycles of liposomal doxorubicin (last 7/1). Oncology note and restaging CT in chart: lung infiltrates and effusions gone. Lesions faded. He feels like himself again - eating better within the limits of the achalasia, no cough, no sweats.

Weight up about 3.5 kg since March.

Exam: palate with faint flat purplish discoloration only. Shins with flat brown-violet macules, no raised lesions. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
- Kaposi sarcoma - treatment complete, good response. Oncology surveillance every 6 months.
- HIV - ID visit in October.
- Achalasia, myopathy - unchanged.
- Tobacco - 1 ppd. Again offered help; he'll stay on the patch.
- CBC, CMP today after chemo.
- FIT overdue (due June) - kit given.
Flu/COVID in October. Check in late fall.

documents.body: Your blood counts have recovered nicely after chemo and your kidney and liver tests are normal.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC
Visit date: 10/22/2024

Follow-up after completing liposomal doxorubicin for KS in July; lesions faded and restaging CT clear per oncology.
March BAL AFB culture final: no growth.
Adherent to bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF.
CD4 318 cells/uL. HIV-1 RNA not detected (<20 copies/mL).

Plan: continue ART. Labs and visit in 6 months. Smoking cessation advised.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, ID verified by name and DOB.

Short check-in. ID note from October in chart: viral load undetectable, CD4 318. No new skin spots he can see, the old ones keep fading. No cough. Swallowing the same on nifedipine ER - slow meals, sleeps propped up. Legs about the same; uses acetaminophen now and then.
Still smoking around a pack a day. Needs patches.

Exam limited to video: comfortable, speaking full sentences, no visible lesions on the face or lips.

A/P:
- Kaposi sarcoma s/p liposomal doxorubicin - oncology surveillance due February.
- HIV - ID every 6 months.
- Achalasia - GI, nifedipine.
- Hereditary myopathy - stable by report; reminded him to rebook neurology.
- Tobacco - patch refilled.
- Turns 50 in December 2025 - lung screening CT then.
- FIT still not returned; he'll mail it.
Office visit in the spring.
